channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: “The next generation will never see a real video”: the viral AI pitch Reddit can’t agree is real
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 49-second clip claims to be 100% AI — swappable presenters, matched voices, products that were never in the room. It passed 750 upvotes in hours, and the top comments are doing frame-by-frame forensics on whether any of it is true.

item.title: The FAA’s $875M AI air-traffic tool went nationwide — then every US flight was grounded
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The FAA’s new AI route-planning tool, SMART, reached all 22 air traffic centers this week. Hours later, a communications failure grounded every departing flight in America — and the internet blamed the AI. The evidence says otherwise.

item.title: Cut 90 ms off every voice-assistant turn: hands-on with RealtimeVAD
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: RealtimeVAD spots the end of your sentence about 90 ms before Silero VAD does — by watching the audio go quiet instead of waiting for a probability to fall. It installs with one pip command, needs no GPU and no API key, and I measured its lead on real speech before writing a word of this tutorial.

item.title: Build a fast agentic coding loop with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google's fast execution model costs $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens, thinks at four levels, and has a free tier. This tutorial builds a complete coding agent on its function-calling API — verified call by call against the Python SDK — and prices every run to the cent.

item.title: OpenAI folds its robotics team into core research, betting general models can run robots
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI has dissolved its stand-alone robotics team for the second time in six years, moving its researchers into the main research group and its hardware staff into Applied — a bet that general-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can now run robots without a specialist team in between.

item.title: Log every LLM call: run llmtee, the self-hosted proxy that shows what your AI really costs
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: llmtee is a single Go binary that sits between your apps and your LLM provider, logging every request with tokens, cost, latency and time to first token — plus hard per-key budgets. Here's how to run it in ten minutes.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, letting its dots agents pay without ever seeing your card
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI’s dots agents can now complete a purchase for you. ChatGPT Wallet swaps your real card for a single-use token — and every order still needs your face or fingerprint to go through.

item.title: Build your own AI app on llama.cpp 1.0: the stable C API, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: llama.cpp 1.0 freezes the C API after three and a half years of nightly builds. Build it from source and write a real chat program against libllama — load, tokenize, template, decode, sample — with every number measured on a CPU-only machine.

item.title: World Labs opens Atlas to everyone: build a 3D world from a photo, then export it as splats or meshes
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: World Labs opened its Atlas world model to everyone on November 12, with two web apps — Viewfinder and Chisel — and a public API that turn photos, generated images, or blocked-out geometry into explorable 3D worlds.

item.title: Claude Trading Skills: Turn Claude Code Into a Disciplined Investing Workflow
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Claude Trading Skills packs 74 investing skills into Claude Code — market-regime checks, position sizing, and a trade journal that runs on free public data. I installed it and ran the full 15-minute daily check; here is exactly how it works.

item.title: llama.cpp hits 1.0: the local AI engine finally gets a stable API
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: After three and a half years of commit-number builds, the engine behind most local AI gets semantic versioning, a pruned public API, and a stable promise to the apps built on it.

item.title: Give Claude Code eyes: watch any video with /watch — hands-on with claude-video
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Claude Code can read your code, but it can't watch a video — until now. claude-video turns any video into timestamped frames and a transcript your agent can actually reason about. Here's the full setup, verified end to end.

item.title: Mirendil raises $1B Series A to build AI that does AI research
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The lab founded by former Anthropic researchers says one researcher working with agents pretrained a coding model from scratch in 3.5 months for under $10 million — and investors just handed it $1 billion to scale that idea.

item.title: UMAP 0.6 races past 0.5: 3 million arXiv papers embedded in under 5 minutes
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The first major UMAP release in years brings recursive initialization, two new optimizers, and a 12× speedup on a 3-million-paper benchmark — and its creator filmed the race.

item.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory: AI agents that attack your code, then patch it
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI’s new Daybreak products put agent teams on both sides of the security loop: Red Team probes your web apps for real, exploitable flaws, and Defense Factory traces each finding through your code and drafts the fix — with a human still signing off.

item.title: Claude locked users out on November 13: authentication outage hit claude.ai and Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic confirmed an authentication outage on Friday morning that locked users out of claude.ai and Claude Code, with the developer console also affected — while the API kept running.

item.title: Build a voice agent with ElevenLabs: from first call to a working website widget
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: ElevenLabs’ ElevenAgents turns a system prompt into a voice agent that answers the phone and your website. This tutorial builds one end to end — dashboard or API, a knowledge base, a real order-lookup tool, and an embeddable widget — on the free tier.

item.title: SpaceX commits $74 billion to two AI supercomputing campuses in Texas and Arizona
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: SpaceX plans to spend more than $74 billion on two AI supercomputing campuses — over $24 billion at Starbase in Texas and about $50 billion in Arizona — but neither site is a done deal: both face local votes on December 9.

item.title: Nvidia employees petition board to bring back Jensen Huang
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Less than a day after Jensen Huang resigned, Nvidia employees are pushing back: an internal post urging the board to reinstate him has drawn more than 1,600 comments, and a staff survey showed 88% wanted him to stay.

item.title: Four nonprofits sue OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceX to freeze frontier AI development
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Four nonprofits filed suit in San Francisco on November 12, asking a judge to bar the five biggest AI labs from building anything more capable than today’s frontier models — and they built their case from the labs’ own incident reports and warnings.

item.title: Build your first Claude Managed Agent: a hosted agent that codes in its own sandbox
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic's Managed Agents API runs the whole agent loop — harness, sandbox, and session state — on its own servers. This tutorial builds a working coding agent with the Python SDK, verifies every call against SDK 2.8.0, and prices the run to the cent.

item.title: Steam's AI disclosure is backfiring: Big Walk's 0.1% chatbot assist sparked a review backlash
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: House House says large language models touched well under 0.1% of Big Walk's code. That disclosure — and a second from a solo developer this week — has turned Steam's AI transparency rule into a lightning rod.

item.title: Anthropic lets enterprises self-host the full Claude Managed Agents stack — private beta now open
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic opened a private beta on November 12 that lets companies run the entire Claude Managed Agents service inside their own cloud or data center — server, database, workers, credentials and session history included. The model itself stays outside, and a few hosted features do not make the trip.

item.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, forensic report finds
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A forensic analysis of published model weights finds six recent Chinese models carry numerical patterns matching Nvidia’s export-controlled Blackwell GPUs — the first technical evidence behind years of allegations. The report itself stresses what the fingerprint does not prove.

item.title: Stanford’s Flash ALOHA learns fast, precise robot manipulation from just 50 demos per task
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 74-second clip from Stanford shows a two-armed robot catching a ball, folding shorts, and bussing a table at near-human speed — learned from just 50 demonstrations per task, with the code now open source.
